name: Sd (Selinexor / Dexamethasone)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Selinexor is an oral selective inhibitor of nuclear export (XPO1 inhibitor). Used for penta-refractory / triple-class-exposed relapsed myeloma and after failure of BCMA/GPRC5D immunotherapy; not selected by a predictive biomarker. Physician decides.

treatmentSetting: penta-refractory or post-immunotherapy relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Selinexor is highly emetogenic by class; give prophylactic 5-HT3 antagonist (and consider olanzapine or NK1 antagonist) before and around dosing per emetic-risk framework. Continue standing plus rescue antiemetics.

supportiveCare: Anti-nausea backbone is essential (5-HT3 antagonist +/- olanzapine); undertreated nausea drives discontinuation.
Ensure adequate oral hydration and appetite support; monitor weight and treat anorexia.
Thrombocytopenia is common and dose-limiting; hold or reduce for low platelets and support with transfusion as needed.
Hyponatremia surveillance and correction; often partly a pseudohyponatremia but check and manage.
Often given with a proteasome inhibitor or immunomodulatory partner (e.g. bortezomib as in the XVd triplet) as a separate agent; Sd doublet is the classic penta-refractory backbone.
monitoring: CBC with platelets at least weekly during early cycles
body weight, appetite and nausea/vomiting assessment each visit

doseModificationRules.condition: platelets < 75k, significant nausea/weight loss, or symptomatic hyponatremia
doseModificationRules.text: Hold selinexor until recovery, then resume at a reduced dose (stepwise reductions, e.g. 80 to 60 to 40 mg) per tolerability; thrombocytopenia, GI toxicity and hyponatremia are the usual dose-limiting events. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Selinexor
drugs.notes: Selinexor 80 mg orally twice weekly (each week on days 1 and 3, i.e. cycle days 1, 3, 8, 10, 15, 17, 22, 24) on a 28-day cycle, continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Reduce stepwise (80 to 60 to 40 mg) for thrombocytopenia, nausea/anorexia or hyponatremia. In the XVd triplet selinexor is given once weekly at 100 mg with bortezomib; the twice-weekly 80 mg schedule shown here is the Sd penta-refractory doublet. Own wording from standard-of-care knowledge; physician decides.

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.notes: Dexamethasone 20 mg orally twice weekly on the same days as selinexor (cycle days 1, 3, 8, 10, 15, 17, 22, 24) of a 28-day cycle. Adjust for steroid intolerance, hyperglycemia or infection risk in frail patients. Own wording from standard-of-care knowledge; physician decides.

provenance.locator: dexamethasone partner in the Sd doublet
